After finishing the explanations of all the rods, he said to me, “Go and tell everyone to repent, and they will live to God. For the Lord took pity and sent me to give everyone the opportunity to repent, although some are unworthy because of their deeds.[a] But the Lord is patient and wants those called through his Son to be saved.”[b]

2. I said to him, “Sir, I hope that everyone who hears this will repent. For I am convinced that each person, on recognizing their own deeds and fearing God, will repent.”

3. He answered me, “Those who repent with their whole heart and cleanse themselves of their previously mentioned wickedness,[c] adding nothing more to their sins, will receive healing from the Lord for their former sins, if they do not waver over these commandments. They will live to God. But those who add to their sins and live in the desires of this age will condemn themselves to death.”[d]

4. “But you, walk in my commandments and live to God. Everyone who walks in them and acts rightly will live to God.”[e]

5. After showing and telling me all these things, he said to me, “I will show you the rest after a few days.”[f]

      are unworthy to be saved because of their deeds.” The Lord’s pity and the offer to everyone are

    reason: textual_variant
    text: '“Their previously mentioned wickedness” follows the bounded Athos/Michigan possessive auton.
      The1891 body conjectures pason, “all”; alternative: “Cleanse themselves of all the previously mentioned
      wickedness.” The possessive is outside restoration brackets in Michigan’s published text, Bonner
      printed p. 114, papyrus p. 54 line 14. The preceding “repent and” remains bracketed in the working
      edition; Michigan partly preserves the repentance verb and following conjunction, with missing letters.
      This is additional Greek evidence, not a full intact sentence.'

    reason: textual_variant
    text: The self-condemnation warning is wholly bracketed in the 1891 working edition as a version-supported

      witnesses; it does not call the whole bracketed span preserved papyrus ink.'

    reason: textual_variant
    text: “And telling” is bracketed in the working Greek. Michigan has a gap of about twelve lines across
      the end of this section and most of the next opening, so cannot certify this complete closing sentence.

  text: 'After finishing the explanations of all the rods, he said to me, “Go and tell everyone to repent,
    and they will live to God. For the Lord took pity and sent me to give everyone the opportunity to
    repent, although some are unworthy because of their deeds.[a] But the Lord is patient and wants those
    called through his Son to be saved.”[b]


    2. I said to him, “Sir, I hope that everyone who hears this will repent. For I am convinced that each
    person, on recognizing their own deeds and fearing God, will repent.”


    3. He answered me, “Those who repent with their whole heart and cleanse themselves of their previously
    mentioned wickedness,[c] adding nothing more to their sins, will receive healing from the Lord for
    their former sins, if they do not waver over these commandments. They will live to God. But those
    who add to their sins and live in the desires of this age will condemn themselves to death.”[d]


    4. “But you, walk in my commandments and live to God. Everyone who walks in them and acts rightly
    will live to God.”[e]


    5. After showing and telling me all these things, he said to me, “I will show you the rest after a
    few days.”[f]'
